name: Bay of Bengal
genZNote: The Bay of Bengal is India's link to Southeast Asia — it's the reason India's 'Act East' trade policy actually has a sea route to act on.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: The largest bay in the world, a north-eastern arm of the Indian Ocean bounded by India and Sri Lanka to the west, Bangladesh to the north, and Myanmar and the Andaman Islands to the east.
Connects southward into the open Indian Ocean and, via the Andaman Sea, toward the Strait of Malacca and Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: India (Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal coastlines), Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and Thailand (at its south-eastern edge).

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: Major ports: Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata/Haldia and Paradip on India's east coast; Chittagong in Bangladesh; Yangon in Myanmar.

A key route for India's trade with Southeast Asia and East Asia, and the maritime leg of India's connectivity projects with Myanmar and Bangladesh (e.g. the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project).
The Sittwe port project in Myanmar is a notable India-backed connectivity initiative in this region.

sections.heading: 🐠 Economic & Ecological Significance
bullets: Home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, shared between India and Bangladesh at the mouth of the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.
One of the world's most cyclone-prone regions — the Bay regularly generates tropical cyclones affecting India, Bangladesh and Myanmar.
Supports major fisheries and is an important region for offshore oil and gas exploration on India's east coast.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Bay of Bengal is the world's largest bay, a north-eastern arm of the Indian Ocean linking India's east coast to Bangladesh, Myanmar and Southeast Asia.
keyFacts: World's largest bay; part of the Indian Ocean.
Borders India's east coast, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka.
Home to the Sundarbans mangrove forest (India-Bangladesh).
commonConfusion: The Bay of Bengal is a bay, not a strait or gulf — it's geographically an arm of the ocean, not a narrow connecting channel.

highYieldFacts: World's largest bay; India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka border it.
Sundarbans mangroves sit at its northern edge.
Major cyclone-generating region for the Indian subcontinent.
commonTraps: Don't confuse the Bay of Bengal (India's EAST coast) with the Arabian Sea (India's WEST coast).
mustRemember: Bay of Bengal = India's east-coast gateway to Southeast Asia; Sundarbans; cyclone-prone.
